slides.headline: October 22, 2008: India sent its first spacecraft to the Moon.
ISRO launched Chandrayaan-1 aboard PSLV-C11 from Sriharikota
slides.body: The 1,380 kg spacecraft carried 11 scientific instruments - from India, the US, UK, Germany, Sweden and Bulgaria - into a transfer orbit before reaching the Moon on November 8, 2008.

slides.headline: Its Moon Impact Probe struck the lunar south pole, and the orbiter made over 3,400 orbits around the Moon.
slides.body: The mission concluded when communication was lost in August 2009 - but it had already made India one of the handful of countries to successfully send a spacecraft to the Moon.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat needs the scientific ambition to leave its own planet, not just orbit it.
slides.body: Chandrayaan-1 proved India's space program could design, build and fly an interplanetary mission - groundwork that led directly to Chandrayaan-2, Chandrayaan-3's lunar landing, and India's growing space ambitions since.
